name: Drafts and cold rooms
symptom: You can feel moving air near baseboards, outlets, or windows, and certain rooms never warm up.
likelyCauses: Air leakage at the attic hatch, top plates, rim joists, and plumbing/wiring chases — the big leaks are almost never at the windows you can feel
Empty or settled wall insulation (very common pre-1965)
Duct runs that starve the far rooms (splits and two-storeys)
auditMeasures: Blower door test puts a number on total leakage and finds where it enters
Thermal camera maps cold wall sections and missing insulation without opening walls
diyFirst: Weatherstrip the attic hatch and exterior doors
Foam-gasket outlet covers on exterior walls
Hold a stick of incense near suspect spots on a windy day — smoke shows the leak
metaDescription: Why rooms feel drafty and cold, what a blower door test finds, DIY first steps, and which Ontario rebates cover air sealing and insulation.

name: Heating bills feel too high
symptom: Winter gas or hydro bills that make you wince — and you're not sure if that's your house or just prices.
likelyCauses: Envelope losses: thin attic, bare basement walls, leaky frame — the house sheds heat as fast as you buy it
Old equipment: mid-efficiency furnaces burn ~20% more gas than condensing units; electric baseboards cost 2–3× what a heat pump would
Oversized or short-cycling equipment wasting energy on starts
auditMeasures: The EnerGuide model splits your bill into envelope vs. equipment losses — so you fix the right one first
Blower door + thermal imaging quantify the envelope's share
diyFirst: Pull 12 months of bills and note your usage (m³ or kWh), not just dollars — our planner benchmarks it against similar homes
Set back the thermostat 3–4°C overnight; a smart thermostat automates it
metaDescription: How to tell whether high heating bills are your house or your equipment, what an energy audit reveals, and the Ontario rebates that cut the fix's cost.

name: Ice dams and icicles
symptom: Thick ice ridges at the roof edge, big icicles, maybe water staining on ceilings after cold snaps.
likelyCauses: Warm indoor air leaking into the attic (bypasses around chimneys, pot lights, hatches) melts roof snow, which refreezes at the cold eaves
Thin attic insulation letting heat conduct through
Blocked soffit ventilation trapping the heat
auditMeasures: Thermal imaging of the ceiling plane finds the exact bypasses feeding the melt
Attic inspection checks insulation depth and ventilation paths
diyFirst: Roof-rake the lower courses after big snowfalls (from the ground — stay off ladders)
Don't rely on heat cables — they treat the symptom, not the leak

fixLadder.step: Top up attic to R-60 + clear soffit baffles

metaDescription: Ice dams are an attic air-leak problem, not a roof problem. What causes them, how an audit pinpoints the leaks, and the rebates that cover the fix.

name: Second floor too hot or too cold
symptom: Bedrooms roast in July and freeze in January while the main floor is fine.
likelyCauses: Leaky, unbalanced ductwork — long second-floor runs lose their air along the way
Attic heat load overhead (thin insulation) in summer
Rooms over garages with under-insulated floors
Single-zone systems fighting two-zone physics
auditMeasures: Duct testing measures leakage; thermal camera finds the under-insulated ceiling and garage-floor sections
Room-by-room heat-loss calculation shows whether the system can ever balance
diyFirst: Seasonal register balancing: partially close main-floor supplies in summer
Check the furnace fan setting — 'on' (continuous) evens temperatures for a few dollars a month

fixLadder.step: Zoning or a ductless head for the problem floor

metaDescription: Why second floors run hot in summer and cold in winter, the duct and attic fixes that actually work, and which Ontario rebates apply.

name: Window condensation and musty air
symptom: Water pooling on window sills, fogged glass, musty smells, maybe mould spots in corners or closets.
likelyCauses: Too much indoor humidity for the ventilation you have — common in tighter 1980s+ homes without an HRV
Cold surfaces (single-pane windows, uninsulated wall corners) hitting dew point
Bathroom/kitchen fans that vent nowhere or never get used
auditMeasures: The audit checks ventilation rates against occupancy and airtightness — the actual ratio that causes condensation
Thermal imaging finds the cold spots where mould starts
diyFirst: Run bath fans 30 minutes after showers; verify they vent outside
Keep winter humidity near 30–40% (a $15 hygrometer tells you)
Don't buy windows to fix a ventilation problem

fixLadder.step: Insulate the cold surfaces (walls/corners) if imaging shows them

metaDescription: Window condensation is usually a ventilation problem, not a window problem. How an audit tells the difference before you spend $20k on glass.

name: Cold, damp basement
symptom: The basement is 5°C colder than upstairs, feels damp, and nobody wants to spend time there.
likelyCauses: Bare concrete walls — uninsulated foundations can shed 20%+ of a home's heat
Rim joist leakage (the draftiest 30 cm in most houses)
Slab moisture migrating through unsealed concrete
auditMeasures: Thermal imaging shows exactly how much wall is losing heat and where moisture concentrates
The audit sequences moisture control before insulation — order matters in basements
diyFirst: Seal rim joists with cut-and-cobble foam or hire it out cheaply
Check grading and downspouts before any interior moisture fix
metaDescription: Why basements run cold and damp, the insulation sequence that avoids mould, and Ontario rebates for basement insulation.

name: House won't stay cool in summer
symptom: The AC runs all day, upstairs never cools, and July bills rival January's.
likelyCauses: Attic heat load — a 60°C attic over a thin insulation layer is a radiant heater aimed at your bedrooms
Duct leakage dumping cooled air into the attic or walls
Aging or oversized AC short-cycling
auditMeasures: Attic inspection + duct testing find the heat path
Cooling load calculation right-sizes replacement equipment
diyFirst: Close blinds on south/west glass through afternoons
Verify attic ventilation isn't blocked

fixLadder.step: Heat pump replacing the AC (cooling + heating in one)

metaDescription: Why upstairs won't cool, the attic and duct fixes that beat a bigger AC, and how a heat pump swap earns Ontario rebates.

name: Thinking about a heat pump
symptom: Your furnace, AC, or baseboards are due — and everyone has an opinion about heat pumps.
likelyCauses: Electric baseboard homes: the strongest case in Ontario — cold-climate heat pumps typically cut heating electricity 40–60%
Gas-heated homes: at current Ontario gas prices the bill case is modest — the wins are AC included, comfort, and emissions; hybrids hedge
Oversizing risk: without a heat-loss calculation, contractors guess — and guesses cost
auditMeasures: A room-by-room heat-loss calculation (the audit's core output) sizes the unit properly
Envelope findings first — insulation can shrink the heat pump you need by a full size class
diyFirst: Collect a year of bills before quotes — sizing from bills beats sizing from square footage
Get quotes for cold-climate units (rated at -25°C 'CC' performance), not just any heat pump

fixLadder.step: Cold-climate heat pump (up to $12,000 HRSP rebate)

metaDescription: Whether a heat pump makes sense for your Ontario home — baseboard vs. gas economics, cold-climate sizing, and the up-to-$12,000 rebate path.

name: Planning solar panels
symptom: You're curious whether your roof is worth panelling — and what the battery rebate actually covers.
likelyCauses: Ontario's HRSP now offers up to $10,000 for solar + battery — the first meaningful provincial support in years
Roof age, orientation, and shading decide viability more than marketing does
Efficiency first: a cheaper-to-run house needs a smaller, cheaper array
auditMeasures: The audit establishes your real consumption baseline — the number a solar quote should be sized against
EnerGuide documentation supports resale value of the whole package
diyFirst: Check your roof's age first — re-shingling under panels later is expensive
Pull your annual kWh from your hydro account before talking to installers

fixLadder.step: Efficiency upgrades that shrink the target

metaDescription: How to plan rooftop solar in Ontario: the $10,000 solar + battery rebate, roof checks, and why efficiency-first sizing saves twice.

name: Buying (or just bought) a home
symptom: You want to know what the house will really cost to run — before you're the one paying its bills.
likelyCauses: A pre-purchase or move-in energy audit reveals insulation, leakage, and equipment condition no home inspection quantifies
CMHC-insured buyers can claim a 25% mortgage-insurance premium refund after $20,000+ of eligible energy renovations
Move-in is the cheapest renovation window — empty rooms make insulation and sealing easy
auditMeasures: Full EnerGuide evaluation with rating and upgrade report — a renovation roadmap priced against rebates
Documentation that supports the CMHC Eco Improvement claim
diyFirst: Ask the seller for 12 months of utility bills — normal in Ontario, revealing everywhere
Book the audit for the week after closing, before furniture arrives

fixLadder.step: Planned retrofit against HRSP + CMHC refund

metaDescription: Why an energy audit belongs in your home purchase: real operating costs, a rebate-priced renovation roadmap, and the 25% CMHC premium refund.
